clauses.name: Data Processing and DPDPA Compliance
clauses.text: Where either Party collects, stores, or otherwise processes personal data of any individual (a 'Data Principal') in connection with this Agreement, that Party shall comply with the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (the 'DPDP Act'), the Information Technology Act, 2000 and the rules thereunder, and all other applicable data-protection laws. (a) PURPOSE AND LAWFUL BASIS: personal data shall be processed only for the specific, lawful purpose for which it is collected and notified to the Data Principal, on the basis of the Data Principal's consent or another lawful basis permitted under the DPDP Act, and shall not be used for any incompatible purpose. (b) NOTICE AND MINIMISATION: each Party shall give the Data Principal a clear notice of the purpose and the data collected, shall collect only such personal data as is necessary for that purpose, and shall take reasonable steps to ensure the data is accurate and complete. (c) SECURITY SAFEGUARDS: each Party shall implement reasonable security safeguards (including access controls, encryption where appropriate, and organisational measures) to prevent personal data breaches, consistent with Section 8 of the DPDP Act and the reasonable security practices required under Section 43A of the Information Technology Act, 2000. (d) BREACH NOTIFICATION: in the event of a personal data breach, the affected Party shall notify the Data Protection Board of India and each affected Data Principal in the manner and within the timelines prescribed under the DPDP Act. (e) RETENTION: personal data shall be retained only for as long as necessary for the notified purpose or as required by law, and shall thereafter be erased, unless retention is mandated by applicable law. (f) DATA PRINCIPAL RIGHTS: each Party shall enable Data Principals to exercise their rights of access, correction, completion, updating, erasure, and grievance redressal as provided under the DPDP Act, and shall designate a contact for such requests. (g) PROCESSORS: any engagement of a Data Processor shall be under a valid contract that binds the processor to obligations no less protective than those in this clause. (h) CROSS-BORDER TRANSFER: personal data shall be transferred outside India only to the extent permitted under Section 16 of the DPDP Act and any restrictions notified by the Central Government. Each Party shall indemnify the other against losses arising from its own breach of this clause.

clauses.name: Indemnification
clauses.text:
Each Party (the "Indemnifying Party") shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the other Party and its directors, officers, employees, and authorised representatives (each an "Indemnified Party") from and against any loss, liability, cost, or expense arising from that Party's breach of this Agreement, breach of confidentiality, infringement or misappropriation of intellectual property rights, negligence, wilful misconduct, or any related third-party claim. The conduct of any claim to which this indemnity applies shall be governed as follows:
(a) the Indemnified Party shall notify the Indemnifying Party in writing as soon as reasonably practicable after becoming aware of a claim for which indemnity is sought, giving reasonable particulars of the claim; a delay in giving notice shall reduce the Indemnifying Party's liability only to the extent it is actually prejudiced by that delay
(b) the Indemnifying Party may, on written notice, assume conduct of the defence of the claim at its own cost using legal advisers reasonably acceptable to the Indemnified Party, and the Indemnified Party shall provide reasonable cooperation, access to relevant records, and assistance at the Indemnifying Party's cost
(c) the Indemnifying Party shall not settle or compromise a claim on terms that impose a non-indemnified liability, an admission of wrongdoing, or an ongoing restriction on the Indemnified Party without that Party's prior written consent, and the Indemnified Party shall not settle or compromise a claim without prior consultation with the Indemnifying Party except where urgent action is reasonably required to mitigate loss
(d) the Indemnified Party shall take reasonable steps to mitigate its loss, and the indemnity shall not extend to loss to the extent caused or increased by the Indemnified Party's own breach, negligence, or failure to mitigate
(e) recovery under this indemnity shall be reduced by any amount actually recovered by the Indemnified Party from insurance or from a third party in respect of the same loss, so that the Indemnified Party is not compensated twice for the same loss

Any dispute, controversy, or claim arising out of or in connection with this Agreement shall first be attempted to be resolved amicably between the Parties. CORE_DATA_PROCESSING_001.title: Data Processing
CORE_DATA_PROCESSING_001.text: Where either Party collects, stores, or otherwise processes personal data of any individual (a 'Data Principal') in connection with this Agreement, that Party shall comply with the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (the 'DPDP Act'), the Information Technology Act, 2000 and the rules thereunder, and all other applicable data-protection laws. (a) PURPOSE AND LAWFUL BASIS: personal data shall be processed only for the specific, lawful purpose for which it is collected and notified to the Data Principal, on the basis of the Data Principal's consent or another lawful basis permitted under the DPDP Act, and shall not be used for any incompatible purpose. (b) NOTICE AND MINIMISATION: each Party shall give the Data Principal a clear notice of the purpose and the data collected, shall collect only such personal data as is necessary for that purpose, and shall take reasonable steps to ensure the data is accurate and complete. (c) SECURITY SAFEGUARDS: each Party shall implement reasonable security safeguards (including access controls, encryption where appropriate, and organisational measures) to prevent personal data breaches, consistent with Section 8 of the DPDP Act and the reasonable security practices required under Section 43A of the Information Technology Act, 2000. (d) BREACH NOTIFICATION: in the event of a personal data breach, the affected Party shall notify the Data Protection Board of India and each affected Data Principal in the manner and within the timelines prescribed under the DPDP Act. (e) RETENTION: personal data shall be retained only for as long as necessary for the notified purpose or as required by law, and shall thereafter be erased, unless retention is mandated by applicable law. (f) DATA PRINCIPAL RIGHTS: each Party shall enable Data Principals to exercise their rights of access, correction, completion, updating, erasure, and grievance redressal as provided under the DPDP Act, and shall designate a contact for such requests. (g) PROCESSORS: any engagement of a Data Processor shall be under a valid contract that binds the processor to obligations no less protective than those in this clause. (h) CROSS-BORDER TRANSFER: personal data shall be transferred outside India only to the extent permitted under Section 16 of the DPDP Act and any restrictions notified by the Central Government. Each Party shall indemnify the other against losses arising from its own breach of this clause.

PRIVACY_DATA_SUBJECT_RIGHTS_001.title: Data Subject Rights
PRIVACY_DATA_SUBJECT_RIGHTS_001.text: In accordance with the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 ('DPDP Act'), data principals (individuals whose personal data is processed) have the following rights: (a) the right to obtain information about the personal data being processed; (b) the right to correction and erasure of personal data; (c) the right to grievance redressal; and (d) the right to nominate another individual to exercise rights in the event of the data principal's death or incapacity. Requests to exercise these rights may be submitted to the Grievance Officer designated herein.

PRIVACY_DATA_RETENTION_001.title: Data Retention
PRIVACY_DATA_RETENTION_001.text: Personal data is retained for no longer than 24 months, and in any event only for as long as the purpose for which it was collected requires. That purpose is Fulfilling customer orders, issuing invoices, arranging delivery and handling returns. Once it is served, or once you withdraw your consent, the personal data is erased or irreversibly anonymised, as Section 8(7) of the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 requires. We retain personal data beyond that point only to the extent a law in force requires it, and we apply technical and organisational measures designed to ensure deletion happens on time.

PRIVACY_COOKIES_001.title: Cookies and Tracking
PRIVACY_COOKIES_001.text: The platform may use cookies and similar tracking technologies to enhance the user experience and collect usage data. Cookies are small data files stored on the user's device. Users may control cookie settings through their browser preferences. The platform uses: (a) essential cookies necessary for the operation of the service; (b) analytics cookies to understand usage patterns; and (c) preference cookies to remember user settings. Users may opt out of non-essential cookies at any time. Processing of data collected through cookies is governed by this Privacy Policy and applicable Indian law.

PRIVACY_GRIEVANCE_OFFICER_001.title: Grievance Officer
PRIVACY_GRIEVANCE_OFFICER_001.text: In accordance with the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 ('DPDP Act') and the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021, the Data Fiduciary has designated a Grievance Officer to address complaints and queries regarding the processing of personal data. The name and contact details of the Grievance Officer are as follows: Name: Ramesh Kulkarni; Designation: Grievance Officer; Email: contact@alpha.example; Address: 1 First Road, Mumbai, Maharashtra 400001. Each Party shall, in performing its obligations under this Agreement, comply with all Applicable Law, and shall obtain and maintain at its own cost every registration, licence, permission, consent, and approval necessary for it to perform those obligations lawfully.
(a) neither Party shall offer, promise, give, request, or accept any undue advantage, whether directly or through a third party, in order to obtain or retain business or any improper advantage, and each Party shall comply with the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 and with any other anti-bribery legislation applicable to it
(b) each Party shall comply with the applicable tax, labour, environmental, and data protection legislation in force from time to time, including the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 where personal data is processed under this Agreement
(c) each Party shall promptly notify the other if it becomes aware of any circumstance that would make performance of this Agreement unlawful, or that would place the other Party in breach of Applicable Law
(d) a Party shall not be required to do anything under this Agreement that would cause it to breach Applicable Law, and shall consult with the other Party in good faith to agree a lawful alternative before treating performance as excused

CORE_LIMITATION_LIABILITY_001.title: Limitation of Liability
CORE_LIMITATION_LIABILITY_001.text:
Subject to the carve-outs below, the aggregate liability of either Party under or in connection with this Agreement, whether arising in contract, tort (including negligence), breach of statutory duty, restitution, or otherwise, shall not exceed the aggregate fees paid or payable under this Agreement during the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim.
(a) neither Party shall be liable for indirect, incidental, special, punitive, exemplary, or consequential loss, or for loss of profits, loss of anticipated savings, loss of opportunity, loss of goodwill, or loss of business, in each case whether or not that loss was foreseeable at the date of this Agreement
(b) the limitations and exclusions in this clause shall not apply to liability arising from fraud or fraudulent misrepresentation, wilful misconduct, breach of the confidentiality provisions of this Agreement, deliberate infringement or misappropriation of intellectual property rights, a Party's payment obligations in respect of amounts properly due, or any liability which cannot lawfully be excluded or limited
(c) the cap in this clause applies to the aggregate of all claims taken together and not to each claim separately, and each Party's liability shall be reduced to the extent that the loss was caused or contributed to by the other Party's own breach, negligence, or failure to mitigate
(d) the Parties confirm that the allocation of risk recorded in this clause is a genuine and reasonable commercial apportionment, negotiated in light of the consideration payable under this Agreement, and that each Party has had the opportunity to price and insure the risk it bears

CORE_INDEMNITY_001.title: Indemnity
CORE_INDEMNITY_001.text:
Each Party (the "Indemnifying Party") shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the other Party and its directors, officers, employees, and authorised representatives (each an "Indemnified Party") from and against any loss, liability, cost, or expense arising from that Party's breach of this Agreement, breach of confidentiality, infringement or misappropriation of intellectual property rights, negligence, wilful misconduct, or any related third-party claim. The conduct of any claim to which this indemnity applies shall be governed as follows:
(a) the Indemnified Party shall notify the Indemnifying Party in writing as soon as reasonably practicable after becoming aware of a claim for which indemnity is sought, giving reasonable particulars of the claim; a delay in giving notice shall reduce the Indemnifying Party's liability only to the extent it is actually prejudiced by that delay
(b) the Indemnifying Party may, on written notice, assume conduct of the defence of the claim at its own cost using legal advisers reasonably acceptable to the Indemnified Party, and the Indemnified Party shall provide reasonable cooperation, access to relevant records, and assistance at the Indemnifying Party's cost
(c) the Indemnifying Party shall not settle or compromise a claim on terms that impose a non-indemnified liability, an admission of wrongdoing, or an ongoing restriction on the Indemnified Party without that Party's prior written consent, and the Indemnified Party shall not settle or compromise a claim without prior consultation with the Indemnifying Party except where urgent action is reasonably required to mitigate loss
(d) the Indemnified Party shall take reasonable steps to mitigate its loss, and the indemnity shall not extend to loss to the extent caused or increased by the Indemnified Party's own breach, negligence, or failure to mitigate
(e) recovery under this indemnity shall be reduced by any amount actually recovered by the Indemnified Party from insurance or from a third party in respect of the same loss, so that the Indemnified Party is not compensated twice for the same loss

CORE_WAIVER_001.title: Waiver
CORE_WAIVER_001.text: No failure, delay, or indulgence by a Party in exercising any right, power, or remedy under this Agreement shall operate as a waiver of that right, power, or remedy, nor shall any single or partial exercise of it preclude any further exercise of that or any other right, power, or remedy. A waiver of any right, power, or remedy under this Agreement is effective only if it is given in writing and signed by or on behalf of the waiving Party, and shall not be treated as a waiver of any subsequent breach or default. The rights and remedies provided under this Agreement are cumulative and are not exclusive of any rights or remedies available under Applicable Law.

CORE_SEVERABILITY_001.title: Severability
CORE_SEVERABILITY_001.text: If any provision or part-provision of this Agreement is or becomes invalid, illegal, or unenforceable under Applicable Law, it shall be deemed modified to the minimum extent necessary to make it valid, legal, and enforceable, and if such modification is not possible, the provision or part-provision concerned shall be deemed deleted. Any modification to, or deletion of, a provision or part-provision under this clause shall not affect the validity and enforceability of the remainder of this Agreement, which shall continue in full force and effect. Where a provision is modified or deleted under this clause, the Parties shall negotiate in good faith to substitute a valid and enforceable provision that achieves, so far as possible, the commercial result originally intended.

CORE_DISPUTE_RESOLUTION_001.title: Dispute Resolution Mechanism
CORE_DISPUTE_RESOLUTION_001.text:
Any dispute, controversy, or claim arising out of or in connection with this Agreement shall first be attempted to be resolved amicably between the Parties. If the dispute remains unresolved within fifteen (15) days of written notice, it shall be referred to arbitration in accordance with the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996. The arbitration shall be conducted by a sole arbitrator jointly appointed by the Parties and, failing agreement within fifteen (15) days of a written request, the arbitrator shall be appointed in accordance with the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996. The arbitration shall be conducted on the following terms:
(a) The seat of arbitration shall be Pune, Maharashtra, and the courts at Pune, Maharashtra shall have exclusive supervisory jurisdiction over the arbitration.
(b) Hearings may be held at Pune, Maharashtra or, where the arbitrator so directs or the Parties agree, by video conference.
(c) The arbitral tribunal shall consist of a sole arbitrator, and the proceedings and the award shall be in the English language.
(d) The award shall be in writing, shall state the reasons on which it is based, and shall be final and binding on the Parties.
(e) The arbitrator shall determine the costs of the arbitration, including the fees and expenses of the arbitrator and the reasonable legal costs of the Parties, in accordance with Section 31A of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996.
(f) Nothing in this clause prevents a Party from applying to a competent court for interim measures of protection under Section 9 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, before or during the arbitral proceedings.

CORE_GOVERNING_LAW_001.title: Governing Law and Jurisdiction
CORE_GOVERNING_LAW_001.text:
This Agreement, and any dispute or claim arising out of or in connection with it, its subject matter or its formation (including non-contractual disputes or claims), shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of India, and where local procedural, registration, or stamp matters are relevant, as applied in the State of Maharashtra.

clauses.name: Cancellation of an Order
clauses.title: Cancellation
clauses.text:
A consumer may cancel an order as follows.
(a) An order may be cancelled at any time before it is dispatched, by the means stated on the platform, and the amount paid shall be refunded in full.
(b) No cancellation charge shall be imposed on a consumer who cancels after confirming a purchase, unless Alpha Industries Private Limited bears a similar charge if it cancels the order unilaterally.
(c) Where Alpha Industries Private Limited cancels an order, it shall inform the consumer of the reason and refund the whole amount paid.
(d) An order for goods made to the consumer's specification, or for perishable goods, may not be cancelled after it has entered production or dispatch, and this is stated on the product page before the order is placed.
(e) Cancellation of an order for services is governed by the terms stated at the time of booking.

legal_basis.note: No e-commerce entity shall impose a cancellation charge on a consumer cancelling after confirming a purchase unless similar charges are also borne by the e-commerce entity
Unfair trade practice

clauses.source: Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020; Consumer Protection Act, 2019
clauses.authoring_note: The symmetry requirement in limb (b) is taken from the E-Commerce Rules and is the provision most often breached in practice. The precise sub-rule number was not verified against the bare Rules and should be pinned by the advocate; the rule-level citation is accurate. Limb (d) requires disclosure BEFORE the order, because a non-cancellable category revealed only afterwards is itself an unfair trade practice.

clauses.name: Returns and Replacement
clauses.title: Returns
clauses.text:
A consumer may return goods as follows.
(a) A request to return goods shall be made within 3 days of delivery, by the means stated on the platform.
(b) Goods that are damaged, defective, not as described, or not fit for the purpose for which they were sold, may be returned within that period, and Alpha Industries Private Limited shall at the consumer's option replace them or refund the amount paid.
(c) Where goods are returned because they are damaged, defective, or not as described, the cost of return shipping shall be borne by Alpha Industries Private Limited.
(d) Where goods are returned for any other reason permitted by this Policy, the cost of return shipping shall be borne by the consumer, and that cost is stated on the platform before the return is requested.
(e) Goods must be returned in the condition in which they were delivered, with their original packaging and any accessory or free item supplied with them, save where they are being returned because they are damaged or defective.

clauses.name: How and When a Refund is Made
clauses.title: Refund Timeline
clauses.text:
A refund is made as follows.
(a) Alpha Industries Private Limited shall effect payment of an accepted refund within 3 days of accepting the request, and in any event within the period prescribed under applicable law.
(b) A refund is made to the payment instrument used for the original payment. Where that is not possible, it is made by another means agreed with the consumer, and never as store credit unless the consumer has chosen store credit.
(c) The refund shall include the amount paid for the goods or services and any delivery charge paid, save where only part of an order is returned, in which case the delivery charge is refunded in proportion.
(d) Alpha Industries Private Limited shall inform the consumer when the refund has been initiated, and shall give a reference by which it may be traced.
(e) Where a refund request is rejected, Alpha Industries Private Limited shall inform the consumer of the reason in writing, and the consumer may raise the matter with the Grievance Officer.

legal_basis.note: Every e-commerce entity shall effect all payments towards accepted refund requests within a reasonable period, or as prescribed under applicable law
Unfair trade practice, including refusing to refund consideration for a deficient service

clauses.source: Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020; Consumer Protection Act, 2019
clauses.authoring_note: Limb (b) forbids a default to store credit. Converting a refund into credit without the consumer's choice is a refusal to refund the consideration and falls within the unfair trade practice definition. The advocate should set the refund window; seven days is common and the RBI's directions on failed transactions impose their own timelines where a payment instrument is involved.

clauses.text:
Alpha Industries Private Limited has appointed a Grievance Officer under Rule 4 of the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020.

(d) Nothing in this Policy affects the consumer's right to approach a District, State, or National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, or any other remedy available in law.

ECOM_REFUND_SCOPE_001.title: Scope
ECOM_REFUND_SCOPE_001.text:
This Policy is published by Alpha Industries Private Limited and takes effect from 2026-09-01 (the "Effective Date"). It sets out how a consumer may cancel an order placed on https://alpha.example, and how a refund is made. It forms part of the information Rule 4 of the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020 requires an e-commerce entity to display.
(a) This Policy applies to Subscription access to a cloud-hosted inventory management platform, with onboarding, data migration and email support.
(b) Words used in this Policy have the meaning given to them in the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.
(c) Nothing in this Policy limits a right the consumer has under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, the Sale of Goods Act, 1930, or any other law, and to the extent this Policy is inconsistent with such a right, that right prevails.
(d) Alpha Industries Private Limited may amend this Policy, and an amendment takes effect when it is published. An order placed before an amendment is governed by the Policy in force when the order was placed.

The Parties represent and warrant that:
(a) The object and consideration of this Agreement are lawful under Section 23 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872;
(b) This Agreement is entered into with free consent under Sections 13–19 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872;
(c) Each Party is competent to contract under applicable law.

ECOM_CANCELLATION_001.title: Cancellation
ECOM_CANCELLATION_001.text:
A consumer may cancel an order as follows.
(a) An order may be cancelled at any time before it is dispatched, by the means stated on the platform, and the amount paid shall be refunded in full.
(b) No cancellation charge shall be imposed on a consumer who cancels after confirming a purchase, unless Alpha Industries Private Limited bears a similar charge if it cancels the order unilaterally.
(c) Where Alpha Industries Private Limited cancels an order, it shall inform the consumer of the reason and refund the whole amount paid.
(d) An order for goods made to the consumer's specification, or for perishable goods, may not be cancelled after it has entered production or dispatch, and this is stated on the product page before the order is placed.
(e) Cancellation of an order for services is governed by the terms stated at the time of booking.

ECOM_RETURN_ELIGIBILITY_001.title: Returns
ECOM_RETURN_ELIGIBILITY_001.text:
A consumer may return goods as follows.
(a) A request to return goods shall be made within 3 days of delivery, by the means stated on the platform.
(b) Goods that are damaged, defective, not as described, or not fit for the purpose for which they were sold, may be returned within that period, and Alpha Industries Private Limited shall at the consumer's option replace them or refund the amount paid.
(c) Where goods are returned because they are damaged, defective, or not as described, the cost of return shipping shall be borne by Alpha Industries Private Limited.
(d) Where goods are returned for any other reason permitted by this Policy, the cost of return shipping shall be borne by the consumer, and that cost is stated on the platform before the return is requested.
(e) Goods must be returned in the condition in which they were delivered, with their original packaging and any accessory or free item supplied with them, save where they are being returned because they are damaged or defective.

ECOM_REFUND_TIMELINE_001.title: Refund Timeline
ECOM_REFUND_TIMELINE_001.text:
A refund is made as follows.
(a) Alpha Industries Private Limited shall effect payment of an accepted refund within 3 days of accepting the request, and in any event within the period prescribed under applicable law.
(b) A refund is made to the payment instrument used for the original payment. Where that is not possible, it is made by another means agreed with the consumer, and never as store credit unless the consumer has chosen store credit.
(c) The refund shall include the amount paid for the goods or services and any delivery charge paid, save where only part of an order is returned, in which case the delivery charge is refunded in proportion.
(d) Alpha Industries Private Limited shall inform the consumer when the refund has been initiated, and shall give a reference by which it may be traced.
(e) Where a refund request is rejected, Alpha Industries Private Limited shall inform the consumer of the reason in writing, and the consumer may raise the matter with the Grievance Officer.

ECOM_GRIEVANCE_REDRESSAL_001.title: Grievance Redressal
ECOM_GRIEVANCE_REDRESSAL_001.text:
Alpha Industries Private Limited has appointed a Grievance Officer under Rule 4 of the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020.
(a) The Grievance Officer is Ramesh Kulkarni, who may be contacted at contact@alpha.example.
(b) The Grievance Officer shall acknowledge the receipt of a consumer complaint within forty-eight hours of receiving it, and shall redress the complaint within one month of receipt.
(c) Where a complaint cannot be redressed within one month, the consumer shall be told the reason and the expected time for resolution before that month expires.
(d) Nothing in this Policy affects the consumer's right to approach a District, State, or National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, or any other remedy available in law.

CORE_DISPUTE_RESOLUTION_001.title: Dispute Resolution Mechanism
CORE_DISPUTE_RESOLUTION_001.text:
Any dispute, controversy, or claim arising out of or in connection with this Agreement shall first be attempted to be resolved amicably between the Parties. If the dispute remains unresolved within fifteen (15) days of written notice, it shall be referred to arbitration in accordance with the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996. The arbitration shall be conducted by a sole arbitrator jointly appointed by the Parties and, failing agreement within fifteen (15) days of a written request, the arbitrator shall be appointed in accordance with the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996. The arbitration shall be conducted on the following terms:
(a) The seat of arbitration shall be Pune, Maharashtra, and the courts at Pune, Maharashtra shall have exclusive supervisory jurisdiction over the arbitration.
(b) Hearings may be held at Pune, Maharashtra or, where the arbitrator so directs or the Parties agree, by video conference.
(c) The arbitral tribunal shall consist of a sole arbitrator, and the proceedings and the award shall be in the English language.
(d) The award shall be in writing, shall state the reasons on which it is based, and shall be final and binding on the Parties.
(e) The arbitrator shall determine the costs of the arbitration, including the fees and expenses of the arbitrator and the reasonable legal costs of the Parties, in accordance with Section 31A of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996.
(f) Nothing in this clause prevents a Party from applying to a competent court for interim measures of protection under Section 9 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, before or during the arbitral proceedings.

CORE_GOVERNING_LAW_001.title: Governing Law and Jurisdiction
CORE_GOVERNING_LAW_001.text:
This Agreement, and any dispute or claim arising out of or in connection with it, its subject matter or its formation (including non-contractual disputes or claims), shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of India, and where local procedural, registration, or stamp matters are relevant, as applied in the State of Maharashtra.
(a) subject to the dispute resolution provisions of this Agreement, the competent courts at Pune, Maharashtra shall have exclusive jurisdiction to settle any dispute or claim arising out of or in connection with this Agreement, and each Party irrevocably submits to that jurisdiction
(b) each Party waives any objection to that forum on the ground of inconvenient forum or that proceedings have been brought in an inappropriate court
(c) the rules of private international law shall not apply to the extent they would result in the application of the law of any jurisdiction other than India
(d) nothing in this clause shall prevent either Party from applying to any court of competent jurisdiction for interim or protective relief, including injunctive relief, to preserve its rights pending resolution of the dispute

clauses.title: Failed Delivery
clauses.text:
Where a delivery cannot be completed, the following applies.
(a) Alpha Industries Private Limited shall attempt delivery at least 3 times, and shall inform the consumer before each attempt by the contact details given with the order.
(b) Where delivery cannot be completed after those attempts, the order is returned to Alpha Industries Private Limited and the amount paid is refunded in accordance with the Refund and Cancellation Policy.

clauses.text:
Any dispute, controversy, or claim arising out of or in connection with this Agreement shall first be attempted to be resolved amicably between the Parties. (e) The arbitrator shall determine the costs of the arbitration, including the fees and expenses of the arbitrator and the reasonable legal costs of the Parties, in accordance with Section 31A of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996.

It sets out how Alpha Industries Private Limited ships and delivers orders placed on https://alpha.example, and forms part of the information Rule 4 of the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020 requires an e-commerce entity to display.
(a) This Policy applies to Subscription access to a cloud-hosted inventory management platform, with onboarding, data migration and email support.
(b) Alpha Industries Private Limited delivers to the areas stated on the platform, and the platform states before an order is placed whether delivery to the consumer's address is available.
(c) Nothing in this Policy limits a right the consumer has under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 or any other law.
(d) Alpha Industries Private Limited may amend this Policy, and an amendment takes effect when it is published. An order placed before an amendment is governed by the Policy in force when the order was placed.

ECOM_SHIPPING_CHARGES_001.title: Shipping Charges
ECOM_SHIPPING_CHARGES_001.text:
Shipping charges are applied as follows.
(a) The shipping charge payable on an order is shown to the consumer before the order is placed, and no charge is added afterwards.
(b) Where a shipping charge is waived above an order value, that value is stated on the platform.
(c) Applicable taxes on the shipping charge are shown separately, and the invoice issued to the consumer complies with Section 31 of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017.
(d) Where cash on delivery is offered, any additional charge for it is shown before the order is placed.
(e) Where an order is cancelled or returned in the circumstances set out in the Refund and Cancellation Policy, the treatment of the shipping charge is as stated in that Policy.

ECOM_DELIVERY_TIMELINES_001.title: Dispatch and Delivery
ECOM_DELIVERY_TIMELINES_001.text:
Orders are dispatched and delivered as follows.
(a) An order is ordinarily dispatched within 3 days of being confirmed, and the expected delivery date is shown to the consumer before the order is placed.
(b) Alpha Industries Private Limited shall give the consumer a means of tracking the shipment once it is dispatched.
(c) Where Alpha Industries Private Limited becomes aware that an order will not be delivered by the expected date, it shall inform the consumer, give a revised date, and allow the consumer to cancel the order and receive a full refund if the revised date is not acceptable.
(d) Delivery timelines are estimates and may be affected by matters beyond Alpha Industries Private Limited's reasonable control, but this does not relieve Alpha Industries Private Limited of its obligation under sub-clause (c) to inform the consumer and offer cancellation.
(e) Risk in the goods passes to the consumer on delivery.

ECOM_DELIVERY_FAILURE_001.title: Failed Delivery
ECOM_DELIVERY_FAILURE_001.text:
Where a delivery cannot be completed, the following applies.
(a) Alpha Industries Private Limited shall attempt delivery at least 3 times, and shall inform the consumer before each attempt by the contact details given with the order.
(b) Where delivery cannot be completed after those attempts, the order is returned to Alpha Industries Private Limited and the amount paid is refunded in accordance with the Refund and Cancellation Policy.
(c) A consumer who refuses delivery of goods that are damaged, defective, or not as described shall receive a full refund, including any delivery charge paid.
(d) Where goods are delivered short, damaged, or in a tampered package, the consumer should report it through the platform within 3 days of delivery, and Alpha Industries Private Limited shall investigate and, where the report is made out, replace the goods or refund the amount paid.
(e) Failure to report within that period does not by itself extinguish a right the consumer has under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.

ECOM_GRIEVANCE_REDRESSAL_001.text:

(a) The Grievance Officer is Ramesh Kulkarni, who may be contacted at contact@alpha.example.
